our_argument_summary: Verdict Self-Contradicted. Argument: N2 (12.6583 h) uniquely requires the moon to have Keplerian orbital eccentricity because the amplitude ratio N2/M2 ≈ 0.19 back-solves to e ≈ 0.055 via the Doodson (7/2)·e coefficient. The dome specifies a moon at fixed 2,534 km altitude and no eccentricity parameter; the gear-motion defense (non-uniform angular velocity on a fixed-radius circle) is preempted in four numbered arguments (no gear equation in code; ε_cam reparametrization has same arity; companion-harmonic constraint L2/M2 and 2N2/M2 kills one-point fit; amplitude sideband requires distance variation, forbidden at fixed altitude). Structural post-hoc failure independently: value tabulated since 1921, no monitor.py entry, no timestamped derivation.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: N2 as the larger lunar elliptic semi-diurnal constituent is standard textbook physics (Doodson 1921; Cartwright-Tayler 1971; Schureman 1958). The dome renames the cause ("local moon") but does not derive N2 amplitude from dome geometry.

holes_found.description: Rounding-precision overclaim. detail_evidence reads: "N2/M2 ≈ 0.19 back-solves to e ≈ 0.054, matching the measured lunar eccentricity e ≈ 0.0549 to better than 1%." Computed: (2/7)·0.19 = 0.05429; (0.0549 − 0.05429)/0.0549 = 1.13%. Using the text’s own rounded 0.054: (0.0549 − 0.054)/0.0549 = 1.64%. Neither number satisfies "better than 1%". This is the same precision-sensitivity issue flagged in c5 hole [1] and it survived the EXP-633 gear-motion patch untouched.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace "to better than 1%" with "to about 1%" (accurate at 1.13%) or restate with more digits ("back-solves to e ≈ 0.0543, matching e ≈ 0.0549 to 1.1%"). Either preserves the argument without the precision overclaim.

holes_found.description: Companion-harmonic ratio 2N2/M2 ≈ 0.024 is slightly low vs the standard tabulation. NOAA CO-OPS 37-constituent equilibrium amplitudes give 2N2/M2 ≈ 0.0253 (Schureman 1958: 2.309/90.812 = 0.0254; Cartwright-Tayler 1971 second-order corrections push higher, ≈0.037, but the CO-OPS/Schureman value is the commonly-cited number). The text’s "≈ 0.024" is defensible at 2-sig-fig precision (some tables round to 0.02-0.024) but a defender familiar with NOAA tables could challenge it. L2/M2 ≈ 0.028 (text) matches canonical 0.0283 (Schureman/CO-OPS) exactly. N2/M2 ≈ 0.191 matches. The 2N2 value is the outlier.
holes_found.recommendation: Change "2N2/M2 ≈ 0.024" to "2N2/M2 ≈ 0.025" to match Schureman 1958 / NOAA CO-OPS 37-constituent tabulation. Optionally add the NOAA CO-OPS URL (https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/publications/harmonic_constituents.html) as a companion citation next to "cross-checked against the NOAA CO-OPS 37-constituent list" so the number can be verified.

stronger_arguments.description: The "epistemic parity" preemption. A dome defender can argue that standard physics also treats lunar eccentricity e ≈ 0.0549 as an empirically-measured orbital parameter, not a first-principles derivation — so the globe model and the dome model are on the same footing. The detail_evidence Third argument already addresses this via the companion-harmonic constraint (a single e simultaneously produces N2/M2, L2/M2, 2N2/M2) but does not explicitly frame it as "epistemic parity is achieved through mechanism-yields-family, not through matching-one-ratio." Making this explicit would preempt the "you’re holding the dome to a stricter standard than the globe" retort in a single sentence.

kernel_of_truth.description: N2 is a genuine spectral peak of the semi-diurnal tide with period 12.6583 h (data/wins.json:051.detail_evidence line 1) — this is confirmed by every long-record tide gauge in harmonic analysis (Schureman 1958; NOAA CO-OPS 37-constituent list, cited at data/wins.json:051.detail_evidence). The dome model correctly notes the observation exists and correctly pairs it with the moon. That the moon is the causative body is standard consensus, not disputed here; the dome shares this correct identification.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Matching a tabulated period at 12.66 h is zero-cost (data/wins.json:051.detail_verdict_text — "tabulated since 1921"); the physical mechanism that generates N2 (Keplerian eccentricity, encoded in the amplitude ratio N2/M2 ≈ 0.19) is what a model has to produce, and the dome produces neither an eccentricity parameter (verified 2026-07-11 by grep against monitor.py, api/current/formulas.json, api/current/predictions.json, inject_ai_layer.py — zero hits) nor a mechanism substitute that reproduces the companion-harmonic ratios L2/M2 ≈ 0.028 and 2N2/M2 ≈ 0.025 from the same single parameter. Correctly labeling the constituent “lunar elliptic semi-diurnal” without any lunar elliptic geometry is precisely the self-contradiction the verdict names.

advocate_mode.best_defense: The globe model does not derive e ≈ 0.0549 from first principles either — it is a fitted orbital parameter of the moon’s Keplerian orbit, essentially a boundary condition of solar system formation. Standard tidal theory INPUTS e and derives the Doodson family; the dome likewise takes N2 at 12.66 h as an observational input and matches it. Both models have a one-parameter dependence on lunar orbital shape. The reviewer’s critique that “the dome has no eccentricity parameter” applies with equal force to the globe: neither derives e from more fundamental principles, both accept it from observation. Furthermore, on a gear-driven local-moon model, an eccentric cam profile has ONE free parameter ε_cam that plays the same role e plays in the globe model — it’s a physical property of the cam, exactly as e is a physical property of the orbit, and matching the observed N2/M2 ratio pins it. Charging that the dome parameter is “renamed” rather than “derived” is exactly what one could say of e in globe theory.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Add one sentence in the Third argument (currently begins “the companion-harmonic constraint kills the one-point fit”): after the L2/M2 and 2N2/M2 ratios, note explicitly: “The epistemic ask is not derivation of e from first principles — the globe model also treats e as an orbital parameter fixed by observation. The ask is that a single parameter simultaneously determine N2, L2, and 2N2 at their observed ratios through a physical mechanism. Keplerian orbital motion does this; a Kepler-shaped cam profile would too by mathematical identity; an arbitrary cam profile cannot without independently tuning each ratio, which multiplies rather than reduces the free-parameter count.” Neutralizes the “epistemic parity” defense without abandoning any part of the current argument.
